edition.note: Current edition prepared on 29 September 2026 in Asia/Kolkata, using verified developments and the latest completed market sessions from 28 September.

india.headline: Northern India floods kill at least 62 as Uttar Pradesh reports widespread damage
india.summary: Days of heavy rain and flooding killed at least 62 people in Uttar Pradesh, injured 46 and damaged more than 1,000 houses, according to state authorities cited by the Associated Press. Schools closed in parts of the state and rescue teams moved residents to safer ground; Odisha also evacuated more than 75,000 people.
india.why: The losses show how late-monsoon extremes can cascade through housing, transport, schooling and emergency services, making drainage, warning systems and resilient local infrastructure immediate public-policy concerns.

india.headline: India's broadband subscriptions rise to 1.101 billion in August
india.summary: Telecom regulator data released by the government showed total broadband subscriptions, including machine-to-machine cellular connections, rising from 1.094 billion in July to 1.101 billion in August 2026, a monthly increase of 0.61%. Fixed wired access grew 1.01%, while fixed wireless access grew 2.68%.
india.why: The mix matters as much as the headline total: faster growth in fixed wireless and wired access changes the economics of last-mile connectivity, network capacity and digital-service delivery.

india.headline: India and France broaden space cooperation around TRISHNA, Gaganyaan and start-ups
india.summary: Indian and French ministers discussed cooperation in human spaceflight, microgravity research, start-ups and joint satellite missions. The Indian government said work on the TRISHNA Earth-observation satellite was progressing and noted continuing French support for Gaganyaan, including consumables and flight-surgeon training.
india.why: The agenda links sovereign space capability with climate observation and a commercial ecosystem, showing how mature bilateral science ties can expand from agencies into research institutions and private firms.

india.headline: Delhi finalizes tighter winter air-pollution measures ahead of the high-risk season
india.summary: A central and Delhi government review set hotspot-specific actions, stronger enforcement against dust, waste burning and industrial emissions, and a city-wide 'No PUCC, No Fuel' campaign at 500 camera-enabled fuel stations. The plan also calls for more monitoring stations and restrictions on high-emitting vehicles and construction during winter periods.
india.why: Delhi's winter pollution is a multi-source systems problem; coordinated deadlines, measurement and enforcement across transport, construction, waste and industry are more consequential than any single emergency restriction.

india.headline: Indian Railways approves Kavach 4.0 across 614.75 route kilometres in Varanasi division
india.summary: Indian Railways approved ₹223 crore to deploy the indigenous Kavach 4.0 automatic train-protection system on 614.75 route kilometres of the North Eastern Railway's Varanasi division. Kavach is designed to prevent signals being passed at danger and to apply brakes automatically when required.
india.why: Scaling automatic train protection converts a safety concept into network coverage; deployment discipline, interoperability and maintenance will determine whether the capital approval produces reliable operational risk reduction.

world.headline: Bangkok floodwaters recede slowly after rains affect about 700,000 people
world.summary: Bangkok authorities said weekend flooding affected roughly 329,000 households, or 700,000 people, while nearly 7,000 people were staying in shelters. All 50 city districts were placed under a flood emergency, and high canal levels, transport disruption and staff shortages complicated drainage and airport operations.
world.why: A dense megacity can remain impaired after rainfall eases because canals, roads, labour access and supply chains are coupled; resilience depends on recovery capacity as well as drainage design.

world.headline: Myanmar military airstrike near Rakhine market reportedly kills at least 49
world.summary: The Arakan Army and a rescue official told the Associated Press that a military airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw township killed at least 49 people and wounded 58. AP said it could not independently confirm the details, and Myanmar's military did not immediately comment.
world.why: The reported attack highlights the civilian cost and verification difficulty of Myanmar's fragmented conflict, especially in areas where armed groups control territory and access is restricted.

world.headline: Renewed Tigray fighting raises fears of a wider Horn of Africa conflict
world.summary: Ethiopia's army chief accused Eritrea of backing Tigray rebels and suggested support from Sudan and Egypt; Eritrea and Sudan denied the allegations. Tigray forces captured the strategic town of Erebti, medical groups reported a surge in wounded patients, and an aid leader estimated that about 150,000 people had been displaced.
world.why: The combination of renewed internal war, contested Red Sea access and accusations among neighbouring states creates escalation paths that extend well beyond Ethiopia's borders.

world.headline: NASA's attempt to boost the Swift observatory ends without raising its orbit
world.summary: NASA said Katalyst Space's LINK servicing spacecraft reached orbit but suffered intermittent communications and attitude-control problems, so the partners scaled back a high-risk attempt to rendezvous with and raise the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. The agency expects lessons from the effort to inform future in-space servicing missions.
world.why: The mission is a useful engineering case: an unsuccessful objective can still expose the interfaces, schedule risks and fault-management practices needed for a viable satellite-servicing ecosystem.

world.headline: WHO recognizes nine Western Pacific healthy-city initiatives
world.summary: The World Health Organization recognized eight cities and one national forum at its 2026 Healthy Cities awards after evaluating more than 150 submissions. The selected programmes addressed issues including ageing, health equity, climate resilience, nutrition, mobility, violence prevention and environmental governance.
world.why: City governments often control the practical levers that join health with transport, housing, data and climate adaptation; sharing measured local interventions can shorten the path from pilot to repeatable public system.

domain1.title: Benchmarking RAW and RGB Restoration in Image Signal Processors
domain1.authors: Zihao Lu, Radu Timofte, Marcos V. Conde
domain1.field: Mobile camera pipelines and image restoration
domain1.summary: A controlled study asks where restoration belongs around a fixed, potentially proprietary ISP: before it in mosaiced RAW or after it in rendered sRGB. Its central result is deliberately nuanced—placement alone is not destiny; matching training data to the distribution at the chosen insertion point is the stronger determinant.
domain1.problem: RAW restoration acts on better-characterized sensor noise and blur before demosaicing, colour processing and tone mapping, while RGB restoration can attack artifacts visible in the final image. Prior comparisons often changed the model, training data, degradation synthesis and ISP together, so apparent RAW-versus-RGB advantages could not be attributed cleanly to placement or training alignment.
domain1.difficulty: A real phone ISP is proprietary, nonlinear and device-specific. Tone curves amplify dark-region noise, demosaicing couples neighbouring samples, and colour correction changes error geometry. A fair comparison therefore needs the ISP held fixed, several sensors and degradation types, comparable restoration capacity, and a distinction between generic RGB models and models trained on the target ISP's actual output distribution.
domain1.idea: Treat the fixed ISP as a black box and separate two axes that are usually conflated: the restoration insertion point and whether the training distribution matches that point. Strategy A restores normalized four-plane RGGB before the ISP; Strategy B restores eight-bit sRGB after it. Generic and target-ISP-aware RGB results are reported separately rather than being blended into one verdict.
domain1.method: The benchmark spans four smartphone groups, two learned ISP proxies and three degradation regimes: noise, blur, and joint noise-plus-blur. Compact RAW restorers including NAFNet and MOFA are trained on calibrated degraded-clean RAW pairs, then passed through a frozen ISP. Generic post-ISP baselines use pre-trained AirNet, PromptIR and MiOIR, while a sensor-specific comparison trains a comparable post-ISP NAFNet directly on outputs from the same frozen Vivo X90 ISP. The ISP is never updated and no restoration model receives gradients through it, preserving the modular black-box assumption.
domain1.results: On Samsung S9 at the blur level, NAFNet before ISP v1 reached 25.99 dB versus 22.49 dB for ISP v1 followed by generic MiOIR, a 3.50 dB gap. On Vivo X90 with noise, the degraded ISP fell from 22.60 to 21.52 dB and pre-ISP NAFNet recovered it to 22.00 dB. Yet the target-ISP-trained RGB model beat the sensor-specific RAW model at all three levels, supporting distribution alignment—not a universal RAW advantage—as the main conclusion.
domain1.care: For camera architecture, the paper argues for evaluating an insertion point together with its achievable supervision. A one-to-two-million-parameter RAW shield may transfer better than a 15–30-million-parameter generic RGB restorer, but a compact post-ISP model can win when trained on the exact rendered artifact distribution. This is directly useful for deciding module boundaries around a closed ISP.
learn: Benchmark placement and training-distribution alignment as separate experimental variables.
A pre-ISP module can shield a fixed renderer from noise and blur with modest model capacity.
Post-ISP restoration becomes compelling when paired data reproduce the target ISP's nonlinear artifacts.
Real-world claims remain limited by a 47-image test split and learned ISP proxies.

domain2.title: ExpoCM: Exposure-Aware One-Step Generative Single-Image HDR Reconstruction
domain2.authors: Aoyu Liu, Zhen Liu, Ziyi Wang, Dian Chen, Bing Zeng, Shuaicheng Liu
domain2.summary: ExpoCM turns single-image HDR reconstruction into a one-step consistency-model problem. It explicitly gives saturated highlights, noisy shadows and trustworthy mid-tones different trajectories, then uses an exposure-guided luminance/chrominance loss to reduce brightness and colour errors without iterative diffusion sampling.
domain2.problem: A single LDR exposure irreversibly clips highlight detail and records very few photons in shadows, while well-exposed regions already contain reliable structure. Conventional regression tends to average plausible solutions; diffusion priors can synthesize detail but are slow and may treat three fundamentally different exposure regimes as though they share one degradation process.
domain2.difficulty: The inverse mapping is spatially heterogeneous and ill-posed: highlights need plausible content generation, shadows need noise-aware recovery, and mid-tones should be preserved rather than reinvented. A useful method must avoid semantic drift and colour bias while reducing the dozens or hundreds of iterative evaluations that make diffusion unattractive for interactive or on-device imaging.
domain2.idea: Construct a soft exposure mask, divide the image into over-exposed, under-exposed and well-exposed regions, and give each region a conditioned consistency trajectory. The model reformulates HDR recovery through a probability-flow ODE but learns to reach the clean endpoint in one evaluation, without teacher distillation. A CIE L*a*b* loss weights luminance and chromaticity according to exposure reliability.
domain2.method: The network first estimates continuous exposure memberships rather than using a single hard clipping threshold. Exposure-aware perturbations then define separate training paths: generative recovery for saturated pixels, denoising-oriented recovery for dark pixels and structure preservation for valid pixels. The one-step consistency objective teaches outputs along these paths to agree at the HDR endpoint. An exposure-guided luminance-chromaticity objective supplies region-dependent penalties in perceptually organized colour space. Evaluation covers HDR-REAL, HDR-EYE and AIM2025, with ablations for uniform, two-mask and full three-mask trajectories.
domain2.results: The full three-mask trajectory raised HDR-REAL PSNR from 21.09 dB for the uniform baseline to 25.84 dB and SSIM from 0.6917 to 0.8282; on AIM2025 it raised PSNR from 27.90 to 28.89 dB and reduced LPIPS from 0.192 to 0.150. One-step inference is reported as more than 400 times faster than 1,000-step DDPM and 20 times faster than 50-step DDIM while attaining state-of-the-art fidelity and perceptual accuracy on the evaluated sets.
domain2.care: The design is a reusable lesson for camera algorithms: degradation-aware spatial routing can spend generative freedom only where measurements have failed. For product use, however, highlight hallucination must be clearly distinguished from recovered evidence, and the reported benchmark speedups do not by themselves establish phone-NPU latency, memory traffic or temporal stability for video.
learn: Exposure failure modes deserve different priors, not merely different scalar weights.
Consistency training can collapse an iterative diffusion path into one network evaluation.
Soft exposure partitions avoid brittle boundaries between clipped, noisy and reliable pixels.
Perceptual colour-space losses can target luminance and chroma errors separately.

outside1.title: Ancient DNA reveals pervasive directional selection across West Eurasia
outside1.authors: Ali Akbari, Annabel Perry, Alison R. Barton, Mohammadreza Kariminejad, Steven Gazal, Zheng Li, Yating Zeng, Alissa Mittnik, Nick Patterson, Matthew Mah, Xiang Zhou, Alkes L. Price, Eric S. Lander, Ron Pinhasi, Nadin Rohland, Swapan Mallick, David Reich
outside1.summary: A very large ancient-DNA time series finds that sustained natural selection over the past ten millennia was far more widespread than a handful of textbook sweeps suggest. The study builds a population-structure-aware statistical model and estimates selection at millions of variants rather than reading migration-driven frequency changes as adaptation.
outside1.problem: Allele frequencies change through selection, drift, migration and population mixture. Ancient Eurasia experienced repeated migrations, so a variant that becomes common later may simply have arrived with a new population. Earlier datasets were too small to separate these mechanisms across time and space with enough power to detect modest, sustained selection.
outside1.difficulty: Ancient genomes are sparse, damaged and unevenly sampled by geography and period. Population structure is correlated with sample age, making ordinary principal-component correction liable to erase the time signal or leave confounding. Linkage disequilibrium also means nearby variants move together, complicating both significance testing and the count of genuinely independent selected loci.
outside1.idea: Fit allele-frequency trajectories with a generalized linear mixed model that represents empirically measured relatedness and asks whether a consistent non-zero selection coefficient explains changes better than population structure alone. Impute missing diploid genotypes, validate the statistic with forward simulations, then group linked significant variants into independent loci and compare signals with modern trait associations cautiously.
outside1.method: The analysis combines 15,836 ancient West Eurasians spanning roughly 18,000 years, including 10,016 individuals with newly reported data, and co-analyses 6,438 present-day people. After extensive quality filtering and imputation, the authors estimate selection coefficients for 9.7 million variants. They calibrate the null empirically, cluster variants in linkage disequilibrium, test trait-class enrichment and perform three complementary tests for coordinated polygenic selection across hundreds of modern genome-wide association studies.
outside1.results: At greater than 99% posterior probability, the study identifies 479 independent loci, or 410 outside the complex HLA region. The median estimated selection magnitude at tag variants is 0.86%, with a 0.43–4.3% range; 62% of genome-wide signals associate with at least one UK Biobank phenotype. At a looser 50% false-discovery threshold, 7,689 non-HLA loci imply more than 3,800 independent episodes, though that estimate is intentionally uncertain.
outside1.care: The paper changes the mental model from rare completed sweeps to many modest allele-frequency pushes. Its strongest lesson is methodological: time-series inference must model mixture before attributing causality. Trait labels come from modern industrial populations, so reported changes in polygenic predictors must not be translated into claims about ancient people's observed cognition, disease or social value.
learn: Migration can mimic selection unless population structure is modeled directly.
A small selection coefficient can create a large frequency change over many generations.
Linkage disequilibrium turns significant variants into fewer independent evolutionary events.
Modern GWAS labels are interpretive aids, not direct reconstructions of ancient phenotypes.

outside2.title: Punctuated decline of human cooperation
outside2.authors: Nicholas Sabin, David Klinowski, Felix Reed-Tsochas
outside2.summary: Five years of group-lending records in Sierra Leone reveal cooperation that decays within each loan cycle, jumps when a new cycle resets attention to joint responsibility, and then decays faster after repeated resets. The pattern suggests motivation and effort fatigue, not simply learning or a planned endgame.
outside2.problem: Repeated social dilemmas often begin cooperatively and deteriorate, but short laboratory games cannot show whether the same mechanism persists for years with meaningful stakes. Competing explanations include rational strategic defection, learning the true incentives, worsening ability to pay, and behavioural decay in motivation or effort.
outside2.difficulty: Field data trade experimental control for realism. Groups self-select, poorly performing groups leave the programme, businesses face financial shocks, and repayments reflect both willingness and ability. The researchers therefore needed stable institutional rules, within-group comparisons across restarts, attrition checks, an outcome less sensitive to payment size, and interview evidence about mechanisms.
outside2.idea: Use joint-liability lending as a natural threshold public-goods game. Every member loses future credit if the group misses full repayment, while each person can try to contribute less than a fair share. A new loan cycle preserves much of the group and contract but re-sensitizes members to collective duties, creating a natural reset that helps distinguish behavioural fatigue from structural change.
outside2.method: The study analyses 47,931 partial or full payments from 1,589 groups containing 7,108 borrowers, producing 31,199 monthly group-level cooperation measures over as many as five years. Group fixed-effects panel models track financial contribution and the timeliness-based cooperative-effort rate within and across cycles. Attrition is tested on continuing-group subsets, while 73 in-depth client interviews and nine staff interviews probe motives, sanctions, shocks and institutional practice.
outside2.results: Among groups that continued, cooperation fell each month on average: financial contribution by 0.64% and cooperative effort by 0.97%, both with P below 0.0001. Across four loan restarts, the immediate rebound averaged 4.24% for financial contribution and 2.87% for cooperative effort, again with P below 0.0001. The rebound remained, but subsequent decline accelerated with each restart.
outside2.care: For teams and institutions, a stable incentive design does not guarantee stable behaviour: attention, motivation and effort can decay even after years of successful cooperation. Resets work but habituate, suggesting that automation, habit formation and changing cues may outperform repeated reminders. Causality is still bounded by one microfinance setting and observational field variation.
learn: Threshold dilemmas differ from linear public-goods games because the collective benefit is all-or-nothing.
Behaviour can decline gradually even when rules, membership and long-term incentives stay stable.
A restart can reveal motivational state by changing salience without changing the contract.
Repeated identical reminders may lose durability through habituation.

remember: Restoration quality depends on where a model is inserted and whether its training distribution matches the artifacts at that point.
Exposure-aware routing is valuable because clipped highlights, photon-starved shadows and reliable mid-tones require different operations.
Population movement can imitate natural selection; time-series genomics needs an explicit structure model before it assigns adaptation.
Cooperation can decay while incentives remain unchanged, and identical resets become less durable as participants habituate.
Urban resilience is a coupled-systems problem: rainfall, drainage, transport, staffing and supply chains fail and recover together.
Safety and environmental approvals matter only when coverage, measurement, maintenance and enforcement turn them into operating outcomes.
The 28 September market session was risk-off overall, but stock-level relative strength still separated platform leaders from more rate- or cycle-sensitive names.
takeaways.explore: Connect the ISP-placement paper with the cooperation study through a shared systems lesson: performance depends on the state presented at an interface, not merely on the nominal rule or module. A restorer trained for the wrong artifact distribution fails even if its architecture is powerful; a cooperative contract weakens when attention and effort drift even if incentives remain sound. A useful next investigation is to design an adaptive camera pipeline that measures distribution drift at each stage, routes pixels by degradation state as ExpoCM does, and triggers retraining or recalibration only when the interface statistics—not just final image scores—cross a defined threshold.
